origin: Researcher redesign, 2026-09-22 -- v1's fixed MinSpikeSizePips threshold produced strong quality but out-of-sample trade frequency collapsed ~85-90% in the calmer 2023-2025 window (EURUSD zero trades in 2023) because a fixed pip bar doesn't adapt to changing ambient volatility. Applies the same fix that worked for london_range_fade v2's volatility filter: compare today's move to a rolling average of ITS OWN recent history (apples-to-apples), not a fixed number or a mismatched-timeframe indicator.
thesis: Same as v1: fade the WM/Reuters 4pm London fix volatility spike. Change is purely in the entry filter -- now relative to recent ambient fix-window volatility instead of an absolute pip count.
broker_clock_conversion: Same as v1: 16:00:00 London = 18:00:00 this broker's server time, constant year-round.

entry.measurement_window: 17:55-18:02 server time (15:55-16:02 London), same as v1
entry.trigger: today's fix-window move >= max(MinSpikeSizePipsFloor, MinSpikeVsAvgMultiplier * rolling average of the last SpikeHistoryWindow trading days' fix-window moves). Falls back to the floor alone until MinHistoryToAdapt days of history exist.
entry.side: sell if price rose into the fix, buy if price fell into the fix
skip_conditions: computed lot size below broker minimum (never rounded up)

stop_loss: spike size * SLMultiplier (1.0 default), beyond entry in the spike's own direction
take_profit: spike size * TPMultiplier (1.0 default), back toward the pre-fix price level

exit.rule: market close 30 minutes (HoldMinutes) after the measurement window closes, regardless of P&L, unless SL/TP hit first

tunable_parameters_to_sweep: MinSpikeVsAvgMultiplier, SpikeHistoryWindow, MinSpikeSizePipsFloor -- v1's MinSpikeSizePips=12 fixed threshold is replaced entirely by this adaptive mechanism. Not yet swept -- v2 baseline uses reasonable starting defaults (multiplier=1.5, window=20, floor=5) pending an in-sample sweep.
success_criteria_for_this_redesign: The specific thing v2 needs to demonstrate that v1 didn't: trade frequency in the out-of-sample (2023-2025) period should NOT collapse relative to in-sample the way v1's did -- if 2023 still goes nearly silent under the adaptive threshold, the redesign hasn't solved the actual problem.

demo_criteria.rationale: Standard day_trading category anchor, unchanged from v1.
